items.reason: The asynchronous legacy writes inherit request cancellation and can be aborted when the handler returns.
Legacy DeleteCollection latency and errors are recorded with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration.
Storage Create and Update failures are incorrectly attributed to the legacy metric.
Delete's success metric uses the object name instead of options.Kind for the kind label.
Delete puts d.Log into the context instead of the enriched per-call logger, losing request fields.
The background legacy writes use a request-derived context and can be cancelled before completing.
The legacy DeleteCollection measurement is incorrectly emitted through the storage metric.
Storage.Create failures are recorded with recordLegacyDuration, misattributing the failed backend.
Storage.Update failures are recorded with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.
Delete's success path puts the object name in the kind label, producing per-object metric series.
Request cancellation propagates into the asynchronous legacy writes and can leave legacy storage out of sync.
Legacy.Update receives raw objInfo rather than an updateWrapper carrying the committed storage result, allowing recomputation against stale legacy state.
Delete returns early on storage NotFound, preventing deletion of objects that exist only in legacy.
The Storage.Create error branch attributes its failure to the legacy metric.
The Storage.Update error branch attributes its failure to the legacy metric.
The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration in the storage metric.
Delete's successful storage measurement uses the object name as the kind label instead of options.Kind.
This describes missing logs for legacy-store errors. Adding those logs would not fix the golden issues concerning logger context, metric attribution, or asynchronous write behavior.
Delete installs the base logger rather than the enriched per-call logger in the context, losing downstream log fields.
The tests share a mock between backends and neither await nor verify asynchronous legacy writes, so removing those writes would still pass.
